key_insight: In a benchmark using clinical trial reports with inserted methodological errors, 15 LLMs detected 53%–99% of major errors across two test sets.
clinical_relevance: The findings suggest a potential role for LLM-assisted review of clinical trial research, not evidence of improved cancer drug discovery or patient outcomes.
method: Tested 15 LLMs, including four open-weight models, on three previously studied randomized trial reports.
Repeated testing on 58 randomized trials published in 2026, including all eligible phase 3 trials.
Scored 1,796 reviews using two blinded LLM judges.
evidence_signal: Major-error detection ranged from 53%–96% on the original reports, versus a previously reported 27% mean for untrained human reviewers, and 58%–99% on the 2026 trials.
watch_item: Models also flagged 14%–29% of error types in control reports without inserted errors, raising concerns about false alarms and the need for expert verification.
paper_title: Large language models detect methodological errors that human peer review misses in clinical trials
